title: Imaging and analysis for simultaneous tracking of fluorescent biosensors in barcoded cells
protocol: Seed 4 × 10^5 HeLa cells in a 35 mm glass-bottom tissue culture dish with imaging medium.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Remove old medium and replace with 1 mL fresh imaging medium 30 min before transfection.
Dilute 1 μg of DNA with 50 μL of serum-free DMEM for each dish.
Dilute 3 μL GenJet™ Transfection Reagent with 50 μL of serum-free DMEM for each dish.
Vortex the diluted GenJet™ Reagent and spin down briefly.
Mix the diluted GenJet™ Reagent with the DNA by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Leave the mixture at room temperature for 15 min.
Add the DNA-GenJetTM complex dropwise onto cells in the 35 mm dishes.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Capture images of mCherry under 633 nm excitation on a Zeiss LSM780-FCS laser scanning confocal microscope.
Capture images of BFP under 405 nm excitation on the same microscope.
Open Zen software.
Switch the objective to the 40× oil lens.
Locate the cells.
Switch to “Acquisition” mode.
Click the “Channel Mode” tab under “Light Path”.
Select 30 positions with at least 6–10 fluorescent cells in each viewing field.
Set the excitation source to the 633 nm laser.
Set spectrum collection range from 561 to 695 nm with pinhole set to 30.2.
Click the “Snap” button to capture the image.
Set the excitation source to the 405 nm laser.
Set spectrum collection range from 371 to 430 nm with pinhole set to 30.2.
Click the “Snap” button to capture the image.
Repeat steps 8-11 until images of all barcodes are collected.
Save the two files.
Name one file with suffix “633Ex” (e.g., [Experiment ID]_633Ex.lsm).
Name the other file with suffix “405Ex” (e.g., [Experiment ID]_405Ex.lsm).
Open image files ([Experiment ID]_633Ex.lsm and [Experiment ID]_405Ex.lsm) in ImageJ.
Import macro “0. Image Processing/make montage.ijm” into ImageJ by dragging or through File>Open.
Stitch together all 30 positions in the macro window.
Run "Make Montage..." with columns set to nPositions, rows set to 1, and scale set to 1.
Rename the images to “633Ex” and “405Ex” respectively by right-clicking them.
Manually select cells using the ImageJ selection tool ensuring each selection contains only one cell without overlapping other cells.
Save the regions of interest (ROIs) in the ImageJ ROI manager by pressing "T".
Click More>Save all in the ROI manager to save the ROIs.
Open and run the script “0. Image Processing/save barcode.ijm”.
Concatenate and save barcode images with RFP on the left and BFP on the right using the script.
Include the barcode labels in file names in the format of “[Experiment ID]_[Subcellular location]_[Barcode]_[Cell index].tif”.
Ensure subcellular locations are labeled as “nucleus”, “membrane”, “nuc_mem”, “cytosol”, or “none”.
Rename ROIs according to their index in the ROI Manager.
Duplicate each ROI from the window "633Ex".
Duplicate each ROI from the window "405Ex".
Combine duplicated images into one stack.
Save combined image as TIFF file with specified naming convention.
Close all windows including "633Ex" and "405Ex".
Run python script to preprocess barcode images.
Crop barcode images according to script settings.
Resize images to 150 × 150 pixels.
Cap outlier (1%) signals in images.
Rescale images to 8-bit format.
Read grayscale images from the barcode directory.
Crop images according to barcode ABCD.
Normalize and clip extreme signals for cropped sections A and B.
Resize cropped sections A and B to 150 × 150 pixels.
Save preprocessed barcodes in the processed images directory.
Examine the images to ensure the training images are of good quality.
Discard images with cells that are deformed or have weak or mislocalized signals.
Train deep learning neural networks.
First, train Model 1 to classify BFP images as None (0), Nucleus (1), or Membrane (2).
Second, train Model 2 and Model 3 to classify mCherry images as None (0), Nucleus (1), Membrane (2), Nuclear membrane (3), or Cytosol (4) in the presence of nuclear and membrane BFP.
Finally, assemble Model 1, 2, and 3 to increase overall accuracy.
Test the models with data not used for training.
Determine the best-performing models and use them for subsequent analysis.
Redo model training for two additional models using “Model 2 training.ipynb”.
Seed 4 × 10^5 HeLa cells in a 35 mm glass-bottom tissue culture dish with imaging medium.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Transfect cells with mCherry-NLS, mCardinal-NLS, or iRFP702-NLS plasmids.
Prepare the DNA-GenJetTM mix by diluting 1 μg of each plasmid with 50 μL of serum-free DMEM for each dish.
Dilute 3 μL GenJet™ Transfection Reagent with 50 μL serum-free DMEM.
Vortex the mixture for 5 seconds and spin down briefly.
Immediately add diluted GenJet™ Reagent to the diluted DNA.
Pipette up and down five times to mix.
Leave the mixture at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Add the DNA-GenJet™ complex dropwise onto cells in the 35 mm dishes.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Turn on the Zeiss LSM780-FCS laser scanning confocal microscope.
Set the stage incubator at 37°C.
Open the Zen software.
Switch the objective to the 40× oil lens and locate the cells.
Select the “Acquisition” tab.
Click the “Lambda Mode” tab under “Light Path.”
Select the 633 nm laser as the excitation source.
Set pinhole to 30.2.
Select a spectrum range of 561–695 nm for collection.
Set resolution to 8.9 nm.
Generate 15 images from 561 to 695 nm with intervals of 8.9 nm.
Seed 2 × 10^5 HeLa cells per well with 2 mL culture medium in a 12-well tissue culture plate.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Transfect cells with the barcode and biosensor plasmids.
Remove the old medium from each well.
Replace with 0.75 mL fresh culture medium 30 min before transfection.
Dilute 0.75 μg DNA with 38 μL of serum-free DMEM for each well.
Vortex the mixture for 5 s and spin down briefly.
Dilute 2.25 μL GenJet™ Transfection Reagent with 38 μL of serum-free DMEM.
Mix diluted GenJet™ Reagent with diluted DNA by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Leave the mixture at room temperature for 15 min.
Add the DNA-GenJet™ complex dropwise onto cells in each well of the 12-well plate.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Remove medium from each well.
Rinse with DPBS and detach cells with Accutase.
Collect cells from all 12 wells and mix them together in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Resuspend cells with imaging medium.
Seed 6 × 10^5 cells per dish in 35 mm glass-bottom dishes.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight.
Remove the old medium from each well on the day of imaging.
Replace with imaging medium.
For EGF stimulation experiments, use serum-free imaging medium to starve cells for 1 h prior to imaging.
Turn on the microscope and set the stage incubator at 37°C.
Place the glass-bottom dish on the stage with the lid removed to allow drug administration during time-lapse imaging.
Open the Zen software.
Switch the objective to the 40× oil lens and locate cells.
Click the “Lambda Mode” tab under “Light Path.”
Select the 633 nm laser as the excitation source.
Set pinhole to 30.2.
Select 561–695 nm for the spectrum range to be collected.
Set resolution to 8.9 nm.
Select 30 positions with at least 6–10 fluorescent cells in each viewing field.
Click the “Snap” button to capture the image.
Save the barcode images from these positions as [Experiment ID]_633Ex.lsm.
Navigate to the “unmixing” panel and load the previously saved reference spectra.
Click “Linear Unmixing” to generate three separate images (mCherry, mCardinal, and iRFP702) for each position.
Save the file as [Experiment ID]_633Ex_Linear unmixing.lsm.
Capture the BFP image for each position under “Channel Mode” using the 405 nm laser as the excitation source.
Set spectrum collection range from 371 to 430 nm with pinhole set to 30.2.
Save the file as [Experiment ID]_405Ex.lsm.
Capture barcode images for each position after BFP image acquisition.
Proceed to imaging of biosensors following barcode image capture.
Acquire time-lapse images every 3 min for a total of 10 frames.
Add EGF after frame 3 during the time-lapse imaging.
Select spectrum range of 458–499 nm for CFP and 508–543 nm for YFP and GFP.
Use the 458 nm laser as the excitation source with a pinhole set to 300.6.
Set the frame rate at 3 min per frame for a total of 10 frames.
Select “Definite Focus” as the focusing strategy.
Start time-lapse imaging.
Lift the incubator lid carefully and add stimulant (e.g., EGF) to the dish immediately after acquiring frame 3 images for all positions.
Save the file as [Experiment ID]_FRET.lsm.
Confirm that there are only four files from the experiment in the folder.
Open the file ending with “FRET.lsm” in ImageJ.
Open the ImageJ macro for image analysis (“2. Barcode identification/Image Analysis.ijm”) using the same method as the last step.
Click “Run” on the macro window to run the macro.
Enter the number of different positions in the microscope images and the number of time points taken per position.
Click “OK” to continue.
Select every cell with visible fluorescence in the combine-YFP window using selection tools.
When finished with selecting cells, click “OK” on the dialog box to continue.
Shrink the size of the selection to only include the cell and not the background for each ROI that includes a single fluorophore biosensor.
Select all the ROIs in the ROI Manager.
Record the intensity in the ROI Manager through More>Multi-Measure>Ok.
Copy the results and use the values to overwrite the YFP values in the [Experiment ID]_ROIData.csv file before performing Excel analysis.
Close the windows.
Open the Barcode Prediction Python GUI (“2. Barcode identification/Barcode reading GUI”).
Execute the Python script to open the GUI: > cd “Your_path/Barcode reading GUI” > python Barcode.py
Click “Browse” to select the models.
Set the default thresholds of models 2 and 3 to both be 0.9.
Click “Load model”.
Open a text editor to create a list of barcodes and save it as a .txt file.
Enter each barcode on a new line in the text file.
Click “Browse” to select the path for the barcode list.
Click “Confirm list”.
Select the folder with barcode images generated previously.
Change the output folder and filename if desired.
Click “Browse” to select the path of the spectrum data from previous steps.
Click “Predict barcode” to run.
This generates the prediction of barcodes.
CloseOperation
Open the Excel template provided on the GitHub page.
Enter barcode/biosensor combinations in the Barcodes sheet.
Record raw measurements in the Raw sheet.
Output model predictions and transposed measurements in the All_Cells sheet.
Open the output file from step 26 (i.e., “modelpred.csv” by default).
Copy the columns [Index] and [Thresholded], and paste them to the columns [Position] and [Barcode] in the sheet [All_cells].
Copy the raw measurements from [Experiment ID]_ROIData.csv.
Paste the raw data into the sheet [Raw].
Copy the raw data in [Raw].
Paste the transposed data into the columns from [YFP1] to [CFP10] in the sheet [All_cells].
Activities will be calculated and updated automatically.
The final result will be in the sheet [Analysis].
